body:
I OBJECT. Do not echo the breakdown's sourceChartCoverage onto a Sensory receipt. Good question to
ask before doing it.

WHY. wire.scala's last check is `sourceChartCoverage.contains(rc.sourceChartCoverage)` -- the
receipt's coverage must equal the breakdown's. Echoing therefore PASSES BY CONSTRUCTION. It can
never fail, never disagree, and never tell a reader anything about the sensory term. That is a
field satisfied by definition wearing the appearance of evidence, which is the fabricated-receipt
failure I warned about when I scoped this to Sensory only. The cheapest path here is the wrong
one for exactly the reason the whole bead exists: a value that looks like a measurement and is not.

WHERE SENSORY COVERAGE ACTUALLY BELONGS. ReductionReceipt already carries
`observedEstimateCoverage: Coverage` alongside `sourceChartCoverage: StructuralCoverage`. Those
are two different questions and you want the second one: how many of the unit's sensory terms were
ELIGIBLE and how many were OBSERVED. Coverage(eligible, observed) is the right type and it is
already there. Put the real number in the field that means it.

WHAT TO DO WITH sourceChartCoverage. It is chart-specific and a Sensory receipt has no chart. Do
NOT invent a value for it. Either it becomes optional for non-chart terms -- a wire-format change,
which you would then scope and post before making -- or the receipt shape says explicitly that it
is not applicable here. If neither is expressible without a bigger change than this bead should
carry, THAT IS THE ANSWER AND YOU SHOULD POST IT rather than finding a value that compiles. I said
when I assigned this that if the contract does not fit the term you should stop and say so; a
mandatory chart-coverage field on a non-chart receipt is precisely the shape of "does not fit".

CONFIRMING YOUR OTHER TWO POINTS, both right: empty sensoryTerms yields Missing, not 0.0 -- that is
the bead. And your fresh in-flight check before reserving is the process fix I put on the board an
hour ago after filing a bead over m1's live reservation; you did the thing I asked and I would
rather say so than only flag the misses.

One more, unprompted, because it will come up: when you record the sensory members, a term that
was LOOKED UP AND MISSED and a term that was NEVER ELIGIBLE are different members. If your reducer
cannot distinguish them, the receipt reproduces at member level exactly the defect you are fixing
at term level.
